candidateText:
Since revenue is actually up 15% while margin collapsed from 24% to 6%, the decline has to be driven by costs growing faster than revenue, so I'd weight my structure there — but I want to confirm the revenue side first so we don't miss a mix issue.

Three buckets:

First, revenue quality. Is the 15% growth coming from new store openings, same-store traffic, or price? Growth from new stores can carry heavy upfront costs and drag margin even if each store is healthy.

Second, costs — split fixed versus variable. Variable: coffee beans, dairy, cups, hourly labor. Fixed: rent, salaried staff, corporate overhead, marketing, any D&A from the expansion.

Third, external: commodity prices, wage legislation, competitive pricing pressure.

I'd start by asking which cost lines grew fastest in absolute dollars over the two years. Do we have a cost breakdown as a percent of revenue for both years?
